root_cause: All secondary sources (Statista, data.gov.my, industry analyses) that reference private medical clinic counts in Malaysia trace back to the MOH Medical Practice Division's registration registry — the same underlying database that produces the Health Facts 2024 figure. There is no independent statistical authority in Malaysia (DOSM, World Bank, academic) that independently counts registered private medical clinics; the MOH MPCB registry is the sole primary administrative data source by law (Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998, Act 586). The '2 source' rubric requirement cannot be met with genuinely independent sources because the data is a single-source administrative record.

reasoning: The 10,495 figure is confirmed verbatim from MOH Malaysia Health Facts 2024 via direct markitdown PDF extraction, making the primary source solid. All secondary sources (Statista, data.gov.my, MIDF) either trace back to the same MOH registry or are inaccessible/paywalled. This is structurally a single-source claim because Malaysia's Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998 designates MOH MPCB as the sole statutory registration authority — there is no independent parallel count. The rubric's '2-source' requirement is appropriate for claims where multiple independent observers could count the same thing, but for administrative registration headcounts sourced from the registrar itself, a single high-quality government source is the epistemic floor. Recommend scoring as High with a note that MOH Health Facts is the statutory registry, not just one opinion among several.
